summary: The core flow is correct in code: select, Position / Scale, ◆ at the start, move later, ◆, type X (which updates the second keyframe through setTransform's upsert), then tap the time pill to play and stop. The white linear keyframe diamonds and the canvas-drag-never-keys warning are both accurate. Needs small fixes, not a redo. (1) Step 4 has no action for when Move is not lit, and misses that Anchor mode also lights Move but removes the ◆. (2) Step 5's 'small diamond at the top' is ambiguous: the rail ◆ is a 38 px button in a vertically centred column, while each X/Y/Z box has a genuinely small 9 px diamond of its own. (3) 'On a computer: it is the same' is wrong for sliding the timeline, because a mouse drag on a clip moves the clip after 4 px. The bottom-left panel claim is right (Studio grid, styles.css:6479), but its citation is wrong. (4) The easing Tip undersells what appears (a graph, a named family row and a six-glyph preset row), and 'tap one' can pick Linear, which changes nothing, or Overshoot/Bounce, which don't soften. (5) The phone hold-to-pick-up-clip pitfall is not mentioned. Several citations have drifted a little (e.g. 7151 is the easing editor's default, not the panel's, which is at 4890; type-in is about 4527, not 4389).

summary: The labels and controls the tutorial names all match the code: 'Tap to add a layer', Audio > 'Import audio', the Volume card, the reversed ruler, 'Fade in (s)'/'Fade out (s)', the mute speaker, and the time pill as play/pause. Three parts are wrong. Step 3 invents an 'audio part' of the timeline: the song is a normal layer placed at the add row and the playhead, and it is selected automatically. Step 7 cannot be done as written on a phone, because the trim buttons are only on the card grid (you must tap '‹ Volume' first) and the video row is hidden while the song is selected. The 'On a computer' paragraph is wrong: the PC hides those buttons and uses the A/S/D keycaps or the D key, and its add line reads 'New layers go here'. Step 1 also fails if a clip is selected, and the tutorial never tells the user to put the playhead at the start before importing.
